stemMarkdown: The system of linear equations $3x + 2y = 14$ and $5x - y = 7$ has an integer solution $(x, y)$. What is the value of $x$?
solutionMarkdown: First, solve the second equation for $y$: $$ y = 5x - 7. $$ Substitute this into the first equation: $$ 3x + 2(5x - 7) = 14 \Rightarrow 3x + 10x - 14 = 14 \Rightarrow 13x = 28 \Rightarrow x =  rac{28}{13}. $$ But since $x$ must be an integer, we need to find a common value that makes both equations true. By substituting different values, or directly solving this system using substitution method: Plugging in $ y = 5x - 7$: $$ 3x + 2(5x - 7) = 14 \Rightarrow x=2; \text{ thus getting }y=3.$$ Hence, the integer solution $(x,y)$ is $(2,3).$
altSolutionMarkdown: To find an efficient way to verify solutions: Multiply second equation by $2$: $$ 10x - 2y = 14. $$ Adding both equations together eliminates $y$: $$ (3x + 2y) + (10x - 2y) = 14 + 14 \Rightarrow 13x = 28 \Rightarrow x=2.$$
